conceptZh: 「門」字變成玩具球門，守門機器人神氣地張腿站好，卻讓慢吞吞的足球從腳間溜進門口。
object: A coral-red glyph-shaped toy doorway, a small mechanical soccer goalkeeper, and one miniature soccer ball.
morph: Begin with the complete, correctly formed 門 as a rigid toy doorway. Its strokes remain unchanged while the ball passes through its lower central opening.
creativeAngle: 不靠門板變形組字，直接讓完整的「門」成為球門；機器人架勢十足，卻漏接慢到不能再慢的球，用兩次低頭確認製造笑點。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked, straight-on shot. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 門, occupying about 70% of frame height with comfortable margins, against a pale cream background and matte pastel floor. Build it from saturated solid coral-red strokes with very shallow toy-plastic depth, preserving the exact front-facing silhouette of a standard Traditional Chinese typeface, including every internal stroke and the lower-right hook. The glyph is a toy doorway serving as a soccer goal; its lower central opening provides the passage. Keep the teaching subject centered and uncropped throughout.

At the opening, a small, clearly mechanical goalkeeper robot with hinged metal legs, oversized toy gloves, and expressive circular LED eyes proudly guards the opening. Its head stays below the internal horizontal strokes. It plants its feet comically far apart and raises its gloves, watching a miniature black-and-white soccer ball roll toward it extremely slowly. Around 1.6 seconds, give the robot a brief confident, motionless anticipation pose. From 2.0–3.1 seconds, the ball gently rolls straight between its planted feet and through the doorway. The robot keeps its gloves raised, looks down at the empty gap, looks behind itself, then looks down again with dramatically enlarged circular eyes: one gentle double-take gag. By 4.4 seconds, it shuffles sideways completely out of frame with its gloves still proudly raised; the ball has disappeared beyond the doorway. From 4.4–8.0 seconds, hold the complete glyph perfectly still, large, centered, unobstructed, and sharply readable. Do not bend, separate, or rearrange any strokes during the action. Use soft lighting, restrained shadows, and bright non-neon colors. The entire scene remains visibly animated and toy-like.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The ONLY spoken line is exactly "門、門、門口". Speak the first 門 around 0.6 seconds, the second 門 around 1.7 seconds, and 門口 around 5.3–6.4 seconds while the finished glyph is fully clear; allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Silent pronunciation directions: 門 = ㄇㄣˊ, pinyin mén; 門口 = ㄇㄣˊ ㄎㄡˇ, pinyin mén kǒu. Use the same mén pronunciation for both isolated utterances and the first syllable of 門口. These Bopomofo and pinyin guides are never spoken or displayed. Add only quiet rolling and soft mechanical joint sounds, with no music or extra dialogue. Only the single target glyph 門 appears as on-screen writing: no vocabulary text, subtitles, logos, written names, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.
direction:
孩子偏好：機器人、蝙蝠俠、搞笑、足球、戰鬥機器人、豬探長、樂高積木、漫威。This clip should use ONE coherent theme, not a crowded crossover. Theme: A soccer robot goalkeeper proudly guards a toy goal/doorway; a very slow ball rolls between its wide-set mechanical feet, prompting a funny double take. Use clearly stylized toys or cartoon animals; costume characters must be obviously toy/robot figures. Keep the character itself and its meaning central; the prop gag is brief and the final glyph remains correct, unobstructed, large and still for at least 3 seconds. No logos or written character names on screen.
PRONUNCIATION LOCK: target 門, Bopomofo ㄇㄣˊ, Mandarin pinyin mén. The ONLY spoken line must be exactly "門、門、門口". Example word is fixed as 門口, pronounced mén kǒu. Do not substitute a word. Both isolated readings and the target syllable inside the word must have exactly the same reading. Include this exact spoken line and these pronunciation guides explicitly in promptEn, stating that Bopomofo/pinyin are silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed. Use clear Taiwanese Mandarin, no extra dialogue, no character catchphrases. Avoid other polyphonic examples or reading alternatives anywhere in the narration instructions. Themes affect the visual gag only, never the spoken vocabulary.

conceptZh: 冒失的小賽車想停在門前，卻煞不住衝過門口，最後小心倒車回到停車墊。
object: A solid coral-red 門 doorway, a squeaky pull-back toy race car, and one small blank parking mat.
morph: The glyph stays correctly formed throughout; the car passes through its lower central opening to demonstrate a doorway.
creativeAngle: 把球門情境改成煞車太晚的停車糗事：車身衝過門，彈簧眼睛還繼續往前晃，才發現停車墊留在後面。最後倒車成功，完整字形保持不動。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, nearly frontal shot. A single correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 門 stands centered as a shallow toy doorway, filling approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use saturated solid coral-red strokes against a light buttery-cream setting, soft lighting, and restrained shadows. Match a standard Traditional Chinese typeface precisely, preserving both upper interior structures, all stroke separations, and the lower-right hook. Its lower central opening is a usable passage. Keep the entire glyph centered, uncropped, and structurally unchanged throughout.

The lead is an original, overconfident turquoise pull-back toy race car with spring-mounted googly eyes, squeaky rubber wheels, and an oversized cheerful grille. Its only supporting prop is a small blank oval parking mat on the floor immediately in front of the doorway. Place the mat low enough that the parked car will remain entirely below the glyph’s lowest strokes. No branding or decorative lettering.

Begin with the car facing away from the camera toward the doorway, eager to park on the mat. During 0.0–1.1 seconds it rolls backward a short distance to wind its pull-back motor, wiggles with confidence, and pauses. At 1.1 seconds it releases itself. Instead of stopping on the mat, it shoots straight across it and through the doorway’s central passage. By 2.3 seconds it brakes on the far side: its body stops, but its googly eyes stretch forward on their little springs, then wobble back into place. Keep this elastic reaction gentle and unmistakably toy-like. At 2.7 seconds both eyes swivel back toward the abandoned parking mat; the grille loses its smug curve for one sheepish beat. From 3.0–4.5 seconds the car carefully reverses through the same opening in two tiny squeaky increments, then settles precisely on the mat. Its eyes brighten with relief. Make the car small enough to pass beneath the interior strokes without touching or obscuring them.

From 4.5–8.0 seconds, hold the entire composition still for 3.5 seconds. The complete glyph is the dominant, sharply readable subject; the tiny parked car and mat sit quietly below it, with no overlap across any stroke. All characters and objects have an unmistakably stylized animated toy appearance. Only the single target glyph 門 appears as on-screen writing; keep the mat and car unlettered and omit subtitles, vocabulary text, logos, watermarks, clutter, and flashing effects.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The exact and only spoken line is "門、門、門口". Pronounce 門 as ㄇㄣˊ, saying the first 門 around 0.3–0.7 seconds, the second around 1.1–1.5 seconds, and 門口 around 5.3–6.3 seconds while the finished glyph remains fully visible. Allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Pronunciation guidance is never displayed or spoken. Add quiet wind-up clicks, soft tire squeaks, and a delicate spring wobble sound beneath the narration; no music or additional dialogue.
